note: Defects that are measured, not suspected. A row with no evidence field is an observation awaiting measurement and is marked severity 'unranked'.

defects.title: One-frame stall of 152 ms during the interactive walkthrough
defects.detail: The QA walkthrough sampled 45 FPS readings across 22 steps: 92 fps average, 6.55 fps minimum. A 6.55 fps sample is a ~152 ms frame. Not yet attributed — candidates are tile decode on the streaming thread, BVH construction on tile register, and the dev-tool spawn path. NOTE 2026-08-08: the walkthrough harness is not a benchmark. Headed Chrome plus a live ffmpeg encode plus ~26 resident MCP node processes produced avg 54 / min 0.08 fps on a build a headless fixed-camera probe measured at 100 avg / 86 1% low. Attribute this defect from the headless probe, not from walkthrough fps.
defects.evidence: evidence/visual/qa-walkthrough/qa-report.json
defects.state: open

defects.title: Simulation order is emergent, and two vehicle registries cannot merge
defects.detail: CORRECTED 2026-08-08. The first version of this entry claimed the city read a stale pause state because ManhattanCity ran before GameLoop. That is false: GameLoop carries R3F renderPriority -100 (on the callback closing line, which is why a grep of the opening line missed it), so it writes rt.paused and the runtime clock before any priority-0 subscriber reads them. Ordering is correct today. What is real: (a) the order is bare integers in separate files with nine of eleven callbacks at the default priority, so their relative order is JSX mount order — undeclared, untested, and changed by moving a line; (b) the frame delta is clamped in six independent places all spelling 1/20 by hand (GameLoop MAX_DT, ManhattanCity, PlayerBody, CityLightingRig, DayCycleRig, SkyRig); (c) sim.registry.vehicles (Map, Phase 3A) and Traffic.vehicles (array, LION) are separate, so a city car cannot become the player car without a second overlapping instance. (c) is the only one with player-visible consequences.
defects.evidence: src/gameplay/simulation.ts; 19 tests; A/B in commit ee58bf966 (100.1 -> 100.0 avg fps, 86.5 -> 86.1 1% low, 3 passes headless)
defects.state: partially fixed — authority adopted by the city stage, one clamp now shared. The two registries (b) and the nine unmigrated useFrame callbacks remain.

defects.title: A night HDR lights the city at every hour; two material systems are dead
defects.detail: AUDITED 2026-08-08, docs/opus/LIGHTING_AUDIT.md. Nothing is fighting over background/fog — sky.js installs and weather.js drives, one subsystem. What is actually wrong: (a) NightEnvironment.tsx:23-58 sets scene.environment to a night HDR with dependency array [gl, scene], neither of which changes after mount, so a night map lights the city permanently regardless of the clock — the exact defect the brief names; (b) getBuildingNightMaterial has one call site, reachable only when ManhattanCity mode==="full", and the game mounts mode="tiles", so it has never rendered a streamed building; (c) SkyRig.tsx is imported by nothing. Streamed BLD_* actually get FacadeMaterial via streamer.injected.
defects.evidence: docs/opus/LIGHTING_AUDIT.md
defects.state: 0C.1 FIXED (18b38e540) — environmentIntensity follows nightFactor; measured 0 at midday, 0.1 at dusk, 0.2 at night. ManhattanCity now shares the canonical curve instead of a private copy with 90-minute-different shoulders. 0C.2 runtime assertion and 0C.3 adopt-or-delete for getBuildingNightMaterial/SkyRig remain.

The working tree carried uncommitted edits I did not make across 7 tracked files (traffic.js, traffic.d.ts, vehicle-control.ts, vehicle-entities.ts, vehicle-lanes.ts, vehicle-replay.test.ts, vehicle-traffic.ts) plus 3 untracked new files (street-nav.js/.d.ts, graph-lane-provider.ts). It is the same consolidation this branch is doing, by a different route: a shared street-nav lane graph and 'ghosts' in Traffic for player-owned vehicles. src/city/traffic.js:109 does not parse, so the city pipeline cannot load and the game cannot boot. vehicle-replay.test.ts — their own Phase 3A determinism gate — also fails. UPDATE 21:45 — traffic.js now parses and the game boots; they also adapted my vehicle-handoff differential test to import pointAt from their street-nav.js, and extended into ManhattanCity.tsx (installLaneProvider + trafficGhosts). Their design is a shared lane graph plus ghosts, which is complementary to the promotion module rather than a duplicate of it. 3 tests in their own new vehicle-session.test.ts still fail on ghost positions (~70 m out).

defects.title: Times Square has no ground; the ocean shows through as a black void
defects.detail: CORRECTED 2026-08-09. The first version of this entry said "the ground plane renders pure black at midday" and blamed cityLightingUniforms.uCityHour defaulting to 21. Both wrong. Raycasting the black region names the mesh: WATER_ocean at y=0, 31-57 m from a camera at y=13.7. It is not a lighting bug and not a road bug — there is simply no island geometry at Times Square, so the sea plane beneath it is what you see. At the actual spawn point (1000, -3000) the same probe hits LAND_manhattan at y=11.99, colour #3f3e3c, exactly as it should. manhattan-collision.ts already documents the cause: "The Phase 2 source data has a genuine hole in the midtown-west band (no buildings, props or subway kiosks west of 6th Avenue — the Times Square plaza included)". The defect is that the hole is not hidden: the ocean should not be visible through missing land. Options are to extend the land mesh, to fill the hole in the Phase 2 source, or to stop rendering ocean inside the island footprint. UPDATE 2026-08-09: measured across all nine dev landmarks — Times Square and the Financial District return no ground; the other seven return 11.5 to 12.12. Teleport now searches outward (src/world/ground-search.ts, 8 tests) and warns rather than using a fallback height over the sea. Both holes are large: Times Square resolves 240 m away, the Financial District 315 m, both onto 11.5 rather than the island 12. That is a guard, not a fix — the hole is Phase 2 content work.
defects.evidence: raycast naming WATER_ocean at Times Square vs LAND_manhattan at the spawn point
defects.state: guarded (8edf0405f) — the underlying land data still has the hole

defects.title: src/world/manhattan-tiles.ts is generated, authoritative-looking, and imported by nothing
defects.detail: 196 generated lines listing 132 building tiles and 61 street tiles, with 'do not edit by hand / regenerate with npm run generate:manhattan-tiles' in its header. Nothing imports it. TileStreamer takes its list from city.json's meta.tiles and meta.street_tiles. The risk is not wasted bytes — it is that the file reads as the source of truth, so a future change made there would have no effect and no diagnostic. Flagged rather than deleted, unlike SkyRig: SkyRig was hand-written code with a named replacement, this is generated data whose generator (scripts/generate-manhattan-tiles.mjs, wired to an npm script) still exists, and deleting generated data could break a workflow not visible from here. The call is: delete both, or make the streamer read it.
defects.evidence: grep for importers returns nothing; streamer.js:35 reads meta.tiles / meta.street_tiles
defects.state: open — needs a decision, not a fix

defects.title: Every vehicle on the hero route is a raw box-and-cylinder placeholder
defects.detail: The brief bans this by name: 'no box vehicle or box pedestrian appears on the hero route'. VehicleRig builds each car from a BoxGeometry body, a BoxGeometry cabin, BoxGeometry headlights, a BoxGeometry accent strip and four CylinderGeometry wheels; rig-resources.ts builds each pedestrian from one 0.42 x 1.7 x 0.26 BoxGeometry. Measured on the loaded hero scene: 101 visible parametric primitives (65 BoxGeometry, 36 CylinderGeometry) across 11 vehicles under the vehicle-rig group, out of 324 visible meshes. Everything else in the scene is authored BufferGeometry. Gate added now (scripts/qa/placeholdercheck.mjs, budget 0) so the number has to go down; it currently fails, which is the honest state. Fixing it is Stage 2 asset work, not a Stage 0 fix. RESOLVED 2026-08-09. The fleet now wears an original authored sportback (scripts/assets/vehicle-mesh.mjs, four LOD tiers, validated through the real GLTFLoader) shared through vehicle-asset-pool.ts, and the crossers wear an original 1.75 m low-poly figure authored in Blender and exported via export_scene.gltf. Measured by scripts/qa/placeholdercheck.mjs against the running game across three stages: 101 visible primitives, then 2 once the vehicles were replaced, then 0. The instrument re-validated on each run — 7/7 injected control boxes detected with 3 of them 2 km out, authored geometry correctly ignored, hidden geometry correctly skipped. Both replacements keep the procedural version as a deliberate fallback: the fetches are async and cars and crossers exist from the first frame, so the alternative is an invisible fleet, and if an asset ever fails to load the primitives come back and this gate fails again, which is exactly what should happen.
defects.evidence: node scripts/qa/placeholdercheck.mjs -> 101 hits, exit 1, instrument validated 7/7 controls incl. 3 at 2 km; evidence/opus/assets/placeholdercheck.json
defects.state: FIXED — placeholdercheck passes at budget 0, verified live

defects.title: A validated detector still gave a false pass, because the sample was wrong rather than the instrument
defects.detail: placeholdercheck first gated on a 150 m radius around the static vision-capture camera and reported 0 placeholders while the scene held 101 — the nearest was 151.1 m away, so it passed by 1.1 m. The instrument was genuinely validated at the time: 7/7 injected control boxes detected, authored geometry correctly ignored, hidden geometry correctly skipped. But every control box was placed at the camera, so the controls proved the detector fired and proved nothing about whether the sample reached where the content lived. Recorded because the standing lesson (validate the instrument before trusting a reading) was followed and was not sufficient: a control must also exercise the filter that decides what gets looked at. The check now defaults to the whole loaded scene, places 3 of 7 controls 2 km out, and asserts that a radius both keeps near controls and drops far ones.
defects.evidence: first run: 0 hits @ radius 150, PASS; scene inspection: 101 primitives under vehicle-rig, nearest 151.1 m
defects.state: closed by design change — kept as a recorded lesson

defects.title: Uncommitted change to the retargeter has flattened the player again — OPUS-009 has regressed in the working tree
defects.detail: scripts/retarget/retarget-glb.mjs and public/models/characters/player/player-clips.glb are both modified in the shared working tree by the other session (OPUS-007). The retargeter defaults were changed from --align-bone root_01 --align-degrees -90 to --align-bone _rootJoint --align-degrees 90, and the clips GLB was regenerated with them (782,404 bytes committed -> 6,357,120 bytes in the tree). Measured with clip-pose.mjs on both files: committed clips put the head 1.001-1.692 m above the left foot across all seven clips with the hip 0.456-0.802 m up, i.e. a standing person; the working-tree clips put the head 0.018-0.313 m above the foot with the hip 0.075-0.208 m, i.e. collapsed into the ground. This is the exact symptom the owner reported from video (character broken and falling to the ground). Two specific reasons the new defaults cannot work: _rootJoint is the holder bone whose 21 animation channels were deliberately stripped across the 7 clips by strip-root-holder-channels.mjs, so aligning on it aligns a bone with no motion; and the comment immediately above the changed lines records the measurement that +90 about z puts the character 1.414 m BELOW the feet, upside down. NOT reverted and NOT staged: the change is uncommitted work in another session, and reverting another agent mid-edit is worse than reporting it. scripts/retarget/clips.test.mjs is failing loudly on it (28 of 39 assertions), which is the gate working as intended. UPDATE same day: re-measured after the other session changed --align-bone back to root_01. The working-tree clips now give head 1.001-1.692 m above the left foot with the hip 0.456-0.802 m, i.e. bit-for-bit the same posture as the committed file, and clips.test.mjs is green again (39/39). Two things are still true and neither is a pose bug: the --align-degrees default is left at 90 while the comment directly above it records -90 as the measured-correct value, so the default and its own documentation disagree even though the current output is right; and the working-tree GLB is 6,357,120 bytes against 782,404 committed, an 8x growth that is not a posture question but should not be committed without knowing what it is.
defects.evidence: node compare of git-lfs HEAD blob vs working tree via clip-pose.mjs; npx vitest run scripts/retarget/clips.test.mjs -> 28 failed
defects.state: resolved in the working tree — re-measured identical to HEAD; one inconsistency left, see detail

defects.title: src/character/PlayerBody.tsx is a complete first-person body that nothing imports
defects.detail: 240 lines exporting PlayerBody(), a procedural humanoid built to match PLAYER_HEIGHT 1.78 m with documented landmarks for head, shoulders, hips, knees and ankles, plus a walk cycle driven by horizontal velocity. Nothing in src imports it; grep across src, scripts and docs finds only its own definition and two mentions in prose. Confirmed at runtime: stagecheck lists every registered system and player-body is absent from the presentation stage, which it would join the moment the component mounted. So first person currently has no visible body at all. Filed rather than deleted, unlike SkyRig: SkyRig had a named live replacement (the Weather engine) so deleting it removed a duplicate, whereas this is the only first-person body implementation in the tree and deleting it would remove a feature rather than a duplicate. It is also made entirely of the primitives 0E.3 bans — BoxGeometry limbs, a SphereGeometry head, a CircleGeometry shadow disc — so if it is ever mounted the placeholder gate will fail on it, correctly. The call is: mount it and replace the primitives with authored art, or delete it and accept a bodiless first person.
defects.evidence: grep -rn PlayerBody src scripts docs -> definition only; scripts/qa/stagecheck.mjs -> presentation stage has 5 systems, player-body not among them
defects.state: open — needs a decision, not a fix

defects.title: 0B.6 scoped wrong in my own notes: entering a city car does not spawn a duplicate, there is no path to enter one at all
defects.detail: My running note said the enter path spawns a second overlapping entity. Read and then measured, that is not what happens. updateEnterPrompt in vehicle-control.ts iterates sim.registry.vehicles only — the Phase 3A registry — so LION traffic cars are not candidates for the prompt, are never offered, and cannot be entered by any path. Measured live with the game driven to screen=playing: Traffic holds 399 cars as {lane, s, v, type, seed, color, alive} across 25,468 lanes (802 sim lanes), while the drivable side is roughly 11 entities (11 groups under vehicle-rig, 101 primitives at about 9 per car). So 399 of the roughly 410 cars in the world are scenery the player can walk through the middle of. scripts/gameplay/vehicles/vehicle-handoff.ts already implements the fix — promoteTrafficCar takes exactly that TrafficCar shape, demoteToTraffic projects a world pose back onto the nearest lane, countRepresentations exists to assert no car is live in both — with tests, and nothing imports it. That makes it the third built-but-unwired module found on this branch after manhattan-tiles.ts (OPUS-010) and PlayerBody.tsx (OPUS-014). Recorded as its own entry rather than silently corrected, because acting on the wrong description would have produced a fix for a bug that does not exist.
defects.evidence: grep: no importer of vehicle-handoff; vehicle-control.ts:587 iterates sim.registry.vehicles; live probe -> traffic.stats {lanes:25468, vehicles:399, simLanes:802}
defects.state: FIXED — vehicle-handoff wired into the enter path; verified live by scripts/qa/handoffcheck.mjs

defects.title: No vehicle in the game could be entered: the interact press was gated on already driving
defects.detail: GameLoop built the vehicle sim input as `driving ? {...full controls...} : NO_VEHICLE_INPUT`, and NO_VEHICLE_INPUT has interact false. Interact is the one input whose entire job is to change whether the player is driving, so gating it on `driving` meant it could only be pressed by someone already in a car. The enter prompt rendered correctly — the player saw "Press E to enter" — and E did nothing. Not specific to city traffic: the same dead branch blocked entry to the nine registry cars too, which is why the missing LION path (OPUS-015) had never been noticed. Fixed by hoisting the edge, `const interactEdge = k.interact && !lastInteract.current`, and feeding it in both branches while leaving throttle, brake, steer, handbrake and horn gated on driving as before. Found only because handoffcheck stood the player on a real car, saw the prompt appear and pressed a real KeyE — a unit test could not have found it, because the pure sim was always correct and the bug lived entirely in what the game loop handed it.
defects.evidence: GameLoop.tsx:169 pre-fix ; only one interact site in the file; handoffcheck before fix -> prompt shown, registry unchanged; after fix -> registry 9 -> 10
defects.state: fixed

defects.title: Capturing traffic.vehicles by reference silently breaks the handoff, because LION replaces the array
defects.detail: The first wiring passed `traffic.vehicles` to installCityTraffic as a value, with a comment defending the choice on the grounds that promotion must splice the live array. The premise was right and the implementation was wrong: traffic.js reassigns the field wholesale in two places — `this.vehicles = keep` when it rebuilds the in-scope set (traffic.js:138), and `this.vehicles = this.vehicles.filter(...)` when it reaps dead cars (traffic.js:327) — so the captured reference is stale from the first rebuild onward. Measured: the pool reported 25,468 lanes and 0 cars against a live fleet of 399. The dangerous form of the same fault is not the empty pool but the near miss — had the capture happened after cars existed, promoteTrafficCar would have spliced an abandoned array while the live car kept circulating, producing exactly the duplicate the module exists to prevent, and reporting success. Fixed by supplying getters so cars, lanes and roadY are re-read on every access, with CityTrafficPool now documenting the requirement and marking the fields readonly. Pinned by a unit test that swaps the array underneath the sim between steps.
defects.evidence: src/city/traffic.js:138,327 reassign this.vehicles; handoffcheck with the captured form -> poolCars 0 of 399; with getters -> 399
defects.state: fixed

defects.title: Every benchmark of the game crashed after sampling, from the consolidation onward — and the baseline on disk describes a build that no longer exists
defects.detail: CORRECTED 2026-08-09, same day as filing. The first version of this entry claimed no run on this branch had ever produced an aggregate. That is false, and the evidence directory says so: shenron-hero-corridor-exterior-stand-high.json and its siblings were written on 2026-08-06, complete with a manhattanProjection. What actually happened is more useful. Those runs predate the one-Manhattan consolidation, when Shenron locations still carried a [lat, lon, ...] spec. The consolidation rewrote those entries to {app, view, note} with no spec at all, and run.cjs built its aggregate with `manhattanProjection: ll2xy(LOCATIONS[location].spec[0], LOCATIONS[location].spec[1])` unconditionally. So from the consolidation onward every Shenron run sampled correctly, printed a real pass line — measured "avg 100.0 fps, 1% low 79.6" on the hero corridor — and then died with "Cannot read properties of undefined" while writing the summary, discarding the run. The failure came after the encouraging output, which is why it survived. Two consequences, both now addressed: the crash is fixed (manhattanProjection only where a spec exists, devView otherwise, filed under the resolved canonical location name), and the aggregates sitting in evidence/performance/phase2o-a are a stale baseline describing cameras that no longer exist — "Dragon Boulevard exterior", "HQ lobby" — which is exactly what 0A.3 was for. New runs are filed under the new canonical names, so the stale set stays readable rather than being silently overwritten.
defects.evidence: run.cjs:578 pre-fix; old aggregates dated 2026-08-06 carry notes.manhattanProjection and view "hero-boulevard"; `--location midtown-street --passes 1 --seconds 5` reproduced the TypeError before the fix and writes notes.devView after it
defects.state: fixed

defects.title: audit:production-scene crashed on a file 0C deleted, and its GLB half had been examining nothing anyway
defects.detail: Two faults in one CI gate. First, activeRenderFiles still listed src/world/SkyRig.tsx, which 0C deleted; readFileSync threw ENOENT and took the whole script — and therefore `npm run check` — down with it, after the useful output had already scrolled past. A stale entry in that list is now a finding rather than a crash, because the list is a claim about what the render path is: when it goes stale the audit stops auditing what it says it audits. Second, and worse, the script printed `Production scene audit passed: {"bytes":0,"files":0,"materials":0,"meshes":0,"primitives":0,"triangles":0}` on every run, because public/assets/production does not exist — the hand-authored production set was deliberately retired in favour of streamed city tiles. So the GLB checks and the manifest cross-check that iterates the same list both examined zero files and reported success. Nothing is failed for that, since the retirement was intentional and the streamed assets are gated by verify:assets and verify-runtime-urls, but the script now says plainly that it had no subject rather than printing a zeros blob that reads like a clean audit. Sixth instance on this branch of a check that measured nothing and reported success. Also worth stating: the source-level primitive check is a JSX-tag grep over a hand-written six-file list, so it never saw the 101 raw primitives on the hero route — VehicleRig builds them with `new THREE.BoxGeometry`, not `<boxGeometry/>`. placeholdercheck.mjs is the real gate for that; this one is a lint and now says so.
defects.evidence: npm run audit:production-scene -> ENOENT src/world/SkyRig.tsx; post-fix output names the missing production root and the 5 render files it did check
defects.state: fixed

defects.title: 0F: every CI gate passes on committed HEAD; the working tree is red only in another session's in-flight edit
defects.detail: Filed when tsc was red with TS2304 "Cannot find name introAudio" — a dropped import in the other session's in-flight IntroSequence edit, which switches the intro from audio to video. They fixed it within the same session; typecheck is now clean. Full gate status measured after that: typecheck PASS, vitest 588 PASS, build PASS, verify:assets PASS (442 models, 496 URLs, 0 missing), verify:production-manifest PASS (11 licensed assets), audit:production-scene PASS, verify:standalone PASS (91 source, 9 build files), npm audit --audit-level=high PASS (0 vulnerabilities). npm run lint reports 12 errors in the working tree, and none are on committed HEAD: three of the four offending files are untracked (scripts/retarget/fix-hand-clipping.mjs, temp_debug.cjs, temp_screenshot.cjs — all created by the other session or as throwaway debug artifacts), so a fresh CI checkout never sees them. The fourth, src/ui/IntroSequence.tsx, fails react-hooks/exhaustive-deps on a `skip` dependency that does not exist in HEAD — `git show HEAD:src/ui/IntroSequence.tsx | grep -c skip` returns 0 — so that error arrives entirely from their uncommitted changes and will land in CI only when they commit it. Not fixed here: their file, their in-flight change. The three untracked files are also left alone rather than deleted — they are not mine, and removing user files needs an explicit path list and approval.
defects.evidence: npm run lint -> 12 errors across 4 files; git ls-files --error-unmatch -> only IntroSequence.tsx is tracked; git show HEAD:src/ui/IntroSequence.tsx has no `skip`; npm audit -> 0 vulnerabilities
defects.state: resolved for HEAD — working-tree lint/typecheck noise is the other session's (OPUS-007)

defects.title: The Blender instance is shared too, and a scene rebuild wipes another session's work in progress
defects.detail: OPUS-007 covers the shared git worktree. The single Blender instance on port 9876 is the same hazard with none of the same protections: there is no branch, no staging area and no diff. Mid-way through authoring vehicle doors, my SHENRON_VEHICLE and SHENRON_PED collections were found empty and the scene replaced with an unrelated street build — facades, fire escapes, shop signs, a wet road — belonging to the other session. Nothing was recoverable from inside Blender. What saved the work is that assets are exported to disk immediately: public/models/vehicles/sportback_lod{0..3}.glb and public/models/characters/pedestrian_lod{0,1}.glb were untouched and still pass scripts/qa/vehicleassetcheck.mjs, including the orientation gate. The .blend was never saved and is not the source of truth; the GLBs and the scripts that generate them are. Practical rules that follow, and that this session will keep to: author into an own collection and never clear or save the file; export immediately rather than leaving work live in the scene; treat a missing collection as "somebody else rebuilt the scene", not as an error; and do not restore by wiping, because the other session is mid-build. Filed rather than worked around because the next person to lose a scene should know it is expected rather than a Blender fault.
defects.evidence: get_objects_summary: SHENRON_VEHICLE and SHENRON_PED both empty, default Collection holding ~250 objects named Escape_*/Far_*/Left_*/Shutter_*; GLBs on disk unchanged and vehicleassetcheck PASS
defects.state: open — a working practice, not a code fix; door art deferred until the scene is free

closed.title: Benchmark 1% low and 0.1% low measured the fastest frames
closed.detail: Ascending frame times with percentile(0.01) returns the smallest frame time. Reported as the low. Blind to stutter and moved the wrong way under increasing stall counts.
closed.fix: fps.low1/low01 (mean of slowest) and fps.low1P99/low01P999 (nearest-rank), 14 tests, old fields renamed RETIRED_*_INVALID in code and baseline.

closed.title: The player's retargeted pose was contorted and static
closed.detail: bake-retarget.py copied absolute bone orientations between rigs with different rest poses (median 78.8 deg from rest across 88 bones), and produced only 2 keyframes per clip against 17-61 in the source — a fixed wrong pose, not an animation.
closed.fix: Replaced with scripts/retarget/retarget-glb.mjs, a rest-delta retargeter in Node with 17 unit tests on the arithmetic. Head 1.414 m above feet (was -0.290), span 0.253 (was 1.410), hands 0.55 m below the head and 0.199 m apart, idle animating. Pipeline no longer needs Blender.
